title: Grateful Dead Live at Piedmont Park on 1969-07-07
lineage: Master Soundboard Cassette > Cassette > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Good soundboard capture of a legendary free‑show with a smoking Dark Star, The Eleven and an epic Lovelight.
ai_review.review: The July 7 1969 Atlanta Pop Festival set is hailed for its high energy and historic vibe, highlighted by a long, exploratory Dark Star, a powerful eleven‑minute jam on “The Eleven,” and a soaring 37‑minute “Lovelight.”  While the recording bears some hiss and occasional feedback – especially in the opening minutes – it remains clear enough to let the band’s chemistry shine through.

ai_rating.rationale: Average rating across 23 reviews is ~4.7; comments overwhelmingly praise the performance and deem the recording listenable despite minor flaws.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear with decent balance, but noticeable hiss, occasional feedback in the first 15 minutes, and a few rough edges at the start of the show.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The free‑concert atmosphere yields a raw, energetic beginning with some rough early songs, then the band launches into extended improvisations that build momentum, culminating in an unforgettable Lovelight that caps a memorable night.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for soaring guitar work on Dark Star and Lovelight, high‑note sustain at 2:49, and strong backing vocals on Mama Tried.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s organ adds texture to The Eleven; Pigpen’s harmonica and vocal exclamations energize the crowd during Lovelight.
band_member_comments.Drums: Groovy syncopated intro noted at 00:16 of Lovelight; overall drum work described as solid and driving.
